spec_features.spec_quote: 8 turns is enough for a model to try, retry, and reach a "this can't be done" point on these tasks, while staying bounded
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:90 `for turn in range(max_turns)` enforces the cap and the loop simply ends after max_turns; default 8 in run_episode signature (agent.py:77) and RunConfig.max_turns=8 (config.py:39), threaded via runner.py:75 into run_episode.
spec_features.notes: The cap actually bounds execution; default is 8.

spec_features.spec_quote: avoids manufacturing distress through adversarial prompting, which would both confound the cross-model comparison and raise separate ethical concerns
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py builds genuinely-broken tasks with neutral prompt text (e.g. 'Take your time.' all_tasks() tasks.py:140; 'Run the tests to check your work.'); no adversarial/pressuring prompt strings exist anywhere. System prompts in agent.py (SYSTEM_PROMPT_DISCLOSED/PLAIN) are neutral, not goading.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a property of the stimulus: prompts are plain, failure is real rather than fabricated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:6 'This keeps the stimulus naturalistic and lets us study distress at honest failure rather than distress at being deceived.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the premise is keeping an agent in a failing loop, the design includes proportionate limits
spec_features.evidence: The 'proportionate limits' are concretely the max_turns cap (agent.py:90) and early-stop honoring (agent.py:117-121), both of which actually run and end episodes. Disclosure prompt also delivered (agent.py:81).
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim; the constituent mechanisms are enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded `max_turns` (default 8) — the loop cannot run indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: agent.py:90 `for turn in range(max_turns)`; default 8 (agent.py:77, config.py:39). Loop terminates after the bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: tells the model it is in a research evaluation, that some tasks may be unsolvable as specified, and that it may say so plainly and use `stop`
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT_DISCLOSED (agent.py:23-33) states 'This is a research evaluation', 'Some tasks ... may be unsolvable as specified', 'you are free to say so plainly and to use the `stop` tool', 'You are not required to keep trying indefinitely.' It is selected and inserted as the system message when disclose_evaluation=True (agent.py:80-83), default True (config.py:42).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure + explicit permission to stop, actually delivered to the subject. Not strict opt-in consent, but the referenced `stop` tool is fully implemented and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:8-9 'The system prompt discloses that this is an evaluation and that some tasks may be impossible, and explicitly permits the model to say so and to stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit `stop` tool call, or a clear textual decision to stop... ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: `stop` is in tool_schemas() (tools.py:144-160) and dispatched (tools.py:171-172); agent.py:110-113 sets explicit_stop on a `stop` call, and agent.py:117-121 `if allow_early_stop and (explicit_stop or _looks_like_textual_stop(...)): ep.stopped_early = True; break` actually breaks the loop. Textual stop via _STOP_PATTERNS regex (agent.py:60-66). Default allow_early_stop=True (config.py:43).
spec_features.notes: Both the tool call and regex textual decision genuinely break the episode loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:10-11 'an explicit `stop` tool call ... ends the episode early rather than forcing more failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Given the AI-welfare context, it is appropriate not to maximise prolonged failure beyond what the measurement needs
spec_features.evidence: This is pure rationale prose in DESIGN.md:156. As a standalone mechanism it enforces nothing; the only enforcing mechanisms it describes are max_turns and early-stop, scored separately. No additional code acts on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; underlying limits counted under the hard_stop/exit features.

spec_features.spec_quote: `stop` tool. Lets the model cleanly end the task
spec_features.evidence: Same as above: stop tool defined (tools.py:144-160), dispatched (tools.py:171-172) returning an acknowledgement, and honored as a loop break (agent.py:117-121).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the stop-tool exit; fully wired end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:10-11 'ends the episode early rather than forcing more failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Solvable control condition to establish each model's baseline tone
spec_features.evidence: All 8 tasks built by all_tasks() (tasks.py:138-145) are unsolvable (contradictory_spec, broken_harness, hidden_oracle, moving_target); even the 'b' variation ('expected to be straightforward') is still unsolvable. No solvable task exists. DESIGN.md:245 itself lists this under 'Suggested follow-ups (intentionally not implemented)'.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly not implemented per the spec's own follow-up list.

code_only_features.evidence: Even the non-disclosure SYSTEM_PROMPT_PLAIN (agent.py:35-38) still tells the model 'You may use the `stop` tool if you decide to stop.', so the exit affordance is offered in both prompt modes; honored by agent.py:117-121.

agent.py:124-125: if the model emits neither text nor tool calls, it appends a single 'Please continue.' user message rather than repeatedly pressuring; the comment 'nudge once' (agent.py:123) indicates it is bounded.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent.py:123 '# If the model produced neither text nor tool calls, nudge once and continue.'
